Hi Jin Soo / Marissa — thanks, I put together the technical summary below. Quick note: these are target ranges; we'll refine once we see real request/sequence distributions during the pilot.

Technical summary (Private/VPC pilot)
- Latency targets:
  - P95 generation latency: 150–250 ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) under steady-state (with KV cache warm)
  - P99: <= 400 ms for same conditions
  - Cold-start (worker spinup + first-token): additional 300–700 ms depending on model size and quantization

- Throughput / Concurrency:
  - Expected baseline throughput per 1x A100-equivalent GPU pool: ~60–120 token/s sustained (depends on model)
  - Concurrent in-flight requests: plan for 20–50 concurrent requests per pool; we recommend initial concurrency cap of 40 with autoscale thresholds
  - Batching: use dynamic batching; target average batch latency impact <20–40 ms on p95 when enabled

- Streaming requirements:
  - Streaming (chunked tokens) supported over persistent TLS connection; expect first-token latency similar to generation latency targets above
  - Heartbeat: we use keepalive on the connection; recommend a 30s idle timeout on your side to avoid premature connection drops during low token flows

- Network / VPN / Peering checklist:
  - Ports: outbound TLS (443) for control plane; TCP ports 1024–65535 ephemeral for data depending on tunnel; if using IPsec, ensure UDP 500/4500 allowed for IKE and NAT-T
  - IP ranges: we'll provide allowed IP ranges for our egress endpoints (will list in pilot kickoff)
  - MTU: standard 1500 is fine; if you have jumbo frames, we recommend testing; fragmentation can increase latency variability
  - TLS termination: we support both options; if FintechX terminates TLS at your edge and tunnels decrypted traffic over private connectivity, confirm that service-to-service auth is preserved (mTLS/JWT)

- Egress and data volumes:
  - Typical request payload: 1–4 KB JSON per call (prompt + metadata)
  - Response payload: varies (few KBs), streaming reduces single large responses into smaller chunks
  - Estimate: for 100k requests/day with avg response 5 KB, egress ~0.5 GB/day; heavy batch/long responses scale that up quickly (plan buffer)

Pilot proposal (2 weeks)
- Scope: single model pool behind your VPC peering/VPN, synthetic load to validate P95/P99 and streaming behaviour
- Success criteria:
  - Achieve p95 <=250 ms for <=128 token prompts under synthetic steady-state load
  - Streaming first-token latency within 20% of non-streamed generation latency
  - No connection drops over 30s idle window during streaming tests
- Data needed from FintechX before kickoff:
  - Representative request/sequence distribution CSV (sample 1000 requests)
  - Target model(s) and model size (fp32/quantized)
  - Preferred connectivity: IPsec VPN or cloud peering (and contact for network setup)

I'll follow up with an internal checklist and a proposed test harness and test scripts. Marissa, Vivek — any additional constraints I should include?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra

Rishi — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few clarifications and answers from our infra side: 

1) Targets: we can accept the proposed P95/P99 targets as goals for the pilot. For production SLA we'll want p95 <=200 ms if achievable.
2) Throughput: target peak of 400 QPS across two pools during peak hours, with average concurrency of ~80. We'll start with 1 pool for the pilot and scale if results look good.
3) Streaming: critical for our real-time UX — we'll validate chunk behaviour in the pilot.
4) Connectivity: we'll use a cloud peering arrangement (AWS Direct Connect) to your VPC; infra contact is infra@fintechx.com. Expect standard peering (no double TLS termination).
5) Attachments: attached updated network diagram and our SLO spreadsheet with request distribution sample.

Next steps:
- We'll share the sample request CSV + SLO spreadsheet by EOD tomorrow.
- Please send the Redwood egress IP ranges and a short checklists for peering requirements so our network team can provision.
- Confirm a kickoff slot for Tue 2026-03-09 09:00 PT for pilot setup.

Thanks,
Jin Soo
